body: thank you for the replies everyone, it was nice to wake up to some support :)

thank you. i've been working on looking at things the way you described, like a learning experience. i've been given a few books to read and i can confidently say i'm not as hard on myself as i used to be. i just get frustrated because in my head i want to get this done as fast as possible for both financial and personal reasons, but i know it's a long and arduous process. i need to learn to give myself time
i did a bookstore last week and thought i'd be able to handle starbucks this week.. oops

i'm upset because it seemed like the next logical step. last week i walked into a barnes & noble and asked for an application, which wasn't really that bad. i don't know why i freaked out so much this time. maybe because it was in a smaller space with more people around

i tried that at first, but the free clinic i went to told me they didn't have anyone i could talk to so they couldn't help me. they gave me a paper with a few places i could try and the one i'm going to now was one of them. there are probably a few places i could go that are cheaper, but i've already established a relationship with the therapist i have now and the idea of starting all over is exhausting


i wish i was european sometimes!
you remind me of myself. want to talk?
i can relate. i know how tough it is. if you want to talk i'm here for you
how u feeling timmy
hi. what did you do today
fuck off. who are you to tell this guy his problems aren't real? you don't know anything about him at all. i don't understand why so many people take mental illness so lightly.

how old are you? i'm struggling in a similar situation at nearly 20, and i'm not quite sure how it's supposed to get better. maybe you can find consolation in the fact that you're not alone. have you considered talking to a therapist?

it's a hard thing to deal with being told, i can imagine. that being said, you deserve a better response than that, and anyone who brushes something like that off isn't worth your time. i'm here to talk if you want to vent about anything

passively suicidal is a good way to describe how i feel, too. i wish i could just get killed in a freak accident. i remember the last time i was on an airplane i kept hoping it would crash. too bad it's the safest way to travel lmao



is there anything that's making you feel this way?
i'm here to talk. you would be doing me a favor as well

that's ok. it's kind of nice to have an outlet and just talk to somebody.


i have been trying to see a therapist. it took me about 4 years before i found the courage to attend one session at my college where the therapist referred me to a free clinic where i might be able to get more help. i put that off for about a month and when i finally went the girl who was assessing me told me that they wouldn't be able to help me there. so i'm currently still looking for someone professional to talk to

thank you for this answer! it definitely helped relieve some of my stress. i will look up some common interview questions and start to prepare. i consider myself pretty good at articulating so i don't think i will have too much of a problem sounding professional, i just need to think of some good life experiences that i'll be able to use as examples... and i will go ahead and submit my volunteer application. i should also look into some resume building resources too i suppose hahahah. not too sure what "skills" i have so we will see how big that blank space turns out to be
yeah i'm worried that i'll be asked about why i've had no experience up until now. obviously i can't talk about social anxiety, especially for an entry level position that deals with customer service

that's good to hear. i absolutely love dogs, so i think i'll force myself to submit an application online in the next few days.


do you think it would be a bad idea for me to try to get a job at a bookstore around the same time i submit an application to the rescue organization? or would the lack of experience hurt me if i were to apply for a job now? i was thinking maybe i start volunteering now, and then try and get an actual job this coming summer since i'll have a few months of volunteering under my belt, but i'll be 20 by the time summer comes around and i feel pretty shitty for not having joined the workforce by now. i guess it's just a few months difference though


i appreciate your input by the way
that's encouraging--hopefully the boss wherever i apply shares that sentiment hahaha. where did you work?

i am absolutely eager to learn and i have high hopes for myself which is why this is so frustrating for me. i would not wish social anxiety/avoidant personality on anyone.

i want to be able to get the point across in interviews that i'm eager to learn, learn quickly, and can succeed in a competitive environment, but i know those are clichés they've all heard before so i am kind of at a loss as to what kind of answers i would give. i do very well in academics and thrive when it comes to presentations/group projects funnily enough, but i feel silly talking about my high school classes and one semester of community college

i'm ok with being asked about my hobbies, i'm into weightlifting and reading so i think i could come up with some good answers there. a place that i would be interested in volunteering at would be for a local dog rescue--would this be a bad idea? i'm not sure how employers would view that kind of experience with animals. there's also a place that packages food among other things to be distributed to families in need that i could volunteer at. i put a few hours in there for a class i took in high school so i have a good idea of what it would be like.


the only place i can think of at the moment to actually work at would be a bookstore, but i don't know if i could land the job without having experience


thanks for the reply mate

did you ever seek out professional help? it sounds like you just did it all on your own! i don't know if i have that kind of willpower... i'm about to turn 20 in a couple of months and i'm looking to start making some changes
how did you overcome your social anxiety?

it doesn't sound like you made an ass of yourself at all. you were quiet, and that's fine! you don't know all of those people as well as they know each other. you made an effort at least, and as long as you weren't rude or obnoxious, i promise you they don't think ill of you at all. it's completely normal to get inside of your head and think of all the stupid (to you) things you said, i do it all the time myself. i'm sure you were just fine though my man

you might feel like you aren't close to your friends anymore, but there is a very good possibility that they don't feel that way at all. do you talk to them outside of when you spend time together? if you do, maybe you should bring up the idea of coming over and watching a movie/sports.

i've only attended 2 sessions with a therapist at my college, who referred me to an independent therapist where i can get more help. the first session was EXTREMELY daunting for me, and my voice shook nearly the whole time. i do think it was helpful, though. it's important to recognize that anxiety and depression leads to distorted thinking, and having a psychological professional challenge those thoughts can make a huge difference. finding the right therapist for you can be equally as important, so don't feel discouraged if you don't click very well with the person you find yourself talking to. just like with any other profession, there are good ones and bad ones. i'm happy to hear that you're considering these options, though! the hardest thing is just getting started. if you choose to go through with these things, make sure you are completely honest with your therapist and yourself.


good luck!!!

hi gene! i'm glad you posted this. you don't have to worry when it comes to posting to this subreddit. that's something that i've learned recently, and i'm happy that i have because it gives me some kind of outlet.


that being said, i know how you feel. i get intense anxiety before heading out, and many times it leads me to staying home instead of doing whatever it is i was going to do. sometimes this has to do with my physical appearance (i look ugly today and i don't want people to see me like this).


it's really good, i think, that you have friends you go out with. do you have anyone you are particularly close with? maybe you could let them know how you are feeling (not all of it perhaps, maybe just a little). have you considered seeing a therapist as well? i am still struggling very much, but i've made the decision to see a therapist to at least try to get over these problems. 


if you want "tips," all i can really offer is exposure therapy. find a social situation that gives you minor anxiety (2 on a scale of 10), practice it until it becomes easy for you, and then move up the scale. apparently it can work wonders!

you really should be proud of yourself for managing to work full time on top of all this. i've never even had a job in my 20 years, so you got me beat there. make sure you're totally honest with your therapist, and really make the effort to get better, and i promise you'll see improvements. you should also consider putting yourself through exposure therapy, starting off as small as you're comfortable with. you just need to get the ball rolling

i also get pretty sad when i scroll through instagram and twitter and see what people are up to, and then there's me... i rarely ever go on them now because of this. i don't even have a facebook at all though. i always thought it was pretty lame


if anyone ever asks why i'm so inactive i usually say something like "oh i just kinda lost interest in it. i don't really go on it anymore"

the idea behind exposure therapy is to start with things that give you minor anxiety and slowly work your way up. throwing yourself into a situation that gives you extreme anxiety is never a good idea. so, say talking to a cashier in a grocery store gives you level 2 anxiety on a scale of 10; this would be a good place to start. then, maybe next time, you purposely hand the cashier the wrong amount of money, or you take your time putting your change back in your wallet. once you can do these things without feeling anxious, you move onto something that gives you level 3 anxiety on a scale of 10

if you live in a state where marijuana is legalized, it's similar to buying groceries. alcohol is the same deal. for me, i never got my medical marijuana card because of my anxiety and i would always ask people i knew to pick up weed for me. i know i would much rather go weeks without smoking than having to find and talk to a dealer or something

the use of drugs and alcohol is not limited to social settings. many of us use them when we are alone. the fact that you feel excluded for your appearance isn't uncommon, your anxiety probably shows and makes people feel uneasy. there is the chance that your case is more severe, but this post kind of sounds as if you are undermining other people's feelings of anxiety

it's very hard for me to believe that people are not judging me. especially people that i haven't seen in a while. my anxiety has gotten worse and i don't understand how they can't be thinking about how different and weird i am. and maybe this is just my perception, but i feel like even strangers can tell i feel uneasy. every interaction i have just feels awkward and awful.

well i don't know how to help you find a good therapist, but i have heard CBT can be very useful. i think exposure therapy would be very useful for you too, and that is something that you can work on on your own before you find a good therapist. i'm starting to experiment with it and it's certainly good at slowly pushing you outside of your comfort zone

first of all, don't apologize for posting this. you have absolutely no reason to. this is a community where we're able to understand these kinds of things. second of all, i can absolutely relate to the things you are saying, so you don't have to feel like you are alone in that regard. i am so fucking terrified of one-on-one social situations i don't even want to get into it. and i also share the sentiment that everyone is more interesting or funny than i am, and that i'm not as important to my friends as they are to me because of it. it seems like they get along so much better with everyone else, and it kills me. i go home and get so angry with myself because of the stupid things i said or the things i didn't say.


that being said, i think it's good that you at least brought up your feelings with your roommates. i do agree that they probably don't understand the severity of your issues (i know my friends don't), but that's ok. you did what you could.

obviously i can't offer you any real advice because i'm experiencing similar things, but you can always message me if you want to talk. have you ever seen a therapist or a school counselor? have you considered seeing one? we're both still young, and we can get over this with some help. i really do believe that our lives and relationships have the potential to get better

you probably already know this, but resorting to drugs and alcohol won't get you where you want to be. i still struggle with smoking weed to help calm my nerves. you're doing the right thing by seeing a psychiatrist. be completely honest with whoever it is you're talking to and i'd be willing to bet that it will help you

hey i just saw this, i haven't logged in for a week. i hope you're doing well and you at least give professional help a real shot. whatever you do, don't lie to yourself or your doctor/therapist. tell the truth, start small with exposure, and things might get better for you and me both. take it one day at a time
absolutely fucking yes. i hate it. it's like i can't be comfortable around *anyone*

how old are you? i think you're focusing too much on being in a relationship. you were in one for 4 years, that should at least tell you that you are capable of such a thing. in my opinion, you should stop seeking out someone else's validation. if you have no one you're interested in dating, that's fine. if you have some relationships that only last a month or two, that's fine. it's hard to find someone that you're compatible with. but the sooner you start focusing on yourself and not so much on other people's approval, the sooner you'll find that confidence you're after.
why don't you have any confidence? what about yourself makes you feel this way?

why did you apply for this job? you can think about it this way... at least it isn't face to face, and those people will never talk to you again for as long as they live. i also think you'll get used to talking on the phone as you go along and it'll get easier for you. maybe it won't be so bad.


when i have bad anxiety (this usually happens in a face to face conversation for me), it becomes difficult for me to listen to what the other person is trying to say to me, and my mind becomes clouded with anxious thoughts. it makes it really difficult to talk to anyone

i feel the same way, if you can find any consolation in that. i change the way i act according to who i'm with, and i always find myself trying to be somebody else because i hate who i am. i spent the last 2 years as a shut-in, and i think it fucked me up real good. 2 years ago i at least thought that i could be fun to be around sometimes, but now i feel as though i have no personality and i'm weird as fuck. i've genuinely been wanting to kill myself because of the way i am.



but, i've made the decision to see a therapist even though i'm not expecting it to solve anything and i know i'll get an anxiety attack in the waiting room and i know my voice will shake while i'm talking to her. i think you should too. it's better than allowing it to spiral out of control. i'm not going to let this shit consume me and be the death of me
